author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Install, test, and roll back a custom Android GPU driver
summary: Use custom AdrenoTools-compatible drivers only on supported Adreno hardware, record a system-driver baseline, verify the package, test one variable, and keep an immediate rollback path.
heroAlt: Mesa 3D gears logo representing the open-source Turnip Vulkan driver stack

blocks.text: A custom driver is an experiment, not an upgrade button

AdrenoTools lets an application load a userspace Vulkan driver without replacing Android's system partition. Turnip packages can fix or expose different behaviours across Adreno generations, but they are not universal: a package built for the wrong GPU generation, Android ABI or Vulkan expectations can crash before a frame appears. Mali and Immortalis devices do not use Turnip packages.

Proceed only when EmuCoreX identifies a supported Qualcomm Adreno GPU and the driver package documents that generation. Keep the system driver selected until a reproducible problem justifies the test.

Back up per-game settings and record the system-driver result in the exact failing scene. Obtain the package from a traceable maintainer, keep its archive intact and record its filename, release page and SHA-256. Do not install Magisk modules or system-wide driver replacements for an app-level comparison.

items: Confirmed Adreno GPU model and Android ABI.
System-driver baseline with screenshots or timing notes.
Traceable AdrenoTools-format driver archive.
Recorded SHA-256 and source page.
A way to reopen settings and choose System driver after failure.

blocks.text: Test one package against the system baseline

items: 1. Download the package from its documented source, calculate SHA-256 and retain the original archive outside the emulator-data folder.
2. In EmuCoreX driver settings, import the package and confirm that its label/generation matches the detected Adreno GPU.
3. Select it for the test game only if the app supports per-game driver choice; otherwise note the global scope before launching.
4. Cold-start the known scene twice, then test a second game that already worked on the system driver.
5. If the package wins on correctness or stability without regressions, keep the evidence and exact hash; otherwise select System driver immediately.

blocks.text: The driver must load without a device-lost loop, compile shaders, render the target effect and remain stable during a warm session. A higher peak frame rate is insufficient when frame pacing, battery drain or another title regresses. Logs should identify the selected driver so a future report can be reproduced.

items: Package target matches the GPU generation.
Driver identity is visible in settings or logs.
Target fault improves in two cold runs.
Known-good comparison game does not regress.
System-driver rollback works without deleting user data.

blocks.text: Select System driver, fully stop EmuCoreX and relaunch before judging recovery. Remove the experimental package from the active driver list only after the system path works. If the app cannot reach settings, clear only the driver-selection preference or reset the affected game profile through the app's recovery path—do not erase memory cards or the whole data folder.

items: Select System driver and restart the app.
Reset the per-game driver override.
Quarantine the failed archive with its hash and result notes.
Reboot Android after repeated Vulkan device-loss errors.
Archive imports but cannot load: wrong ABI, package layout or GPU generation.
One game improves, another crashes: keep the package game-specific or reject it.
Performance rises only while cool: driver changed thermal behaviour, not sustainable capacity.
No rollback record: experimental packages become impossible to distinguish later.

blocks.text: Keep a small driver ledger: package, source, hash, GPU, Android build, tested games and outcome. Replace an accepted package only after rerunning the same baseline. This makes custom drivers reversible engineering tools instead of a growing pile of anonymous ZIP files.
